facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Accept this my praise, Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati, Shutudri, Parushni
facts.text: The Nadistuti Sukta in the tenth mandala of the Rigveda enumerates the Saraswati River in geographic order between the Yamuna in the east and the Shutudri (Sutlej) in the west.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Pure in her course from the mountains to the ocean, she has sustained the living creation with her milk and streams.
facts.text: The Rigveda describes the Saraswati as a mighty and purifying river that flows directly from the mountains down into the sea.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: At Vinasana the river Sarasvati had formerly disappeared in consequence of her contempt for the Nishadas and others.
facts.text: The Mahabharata records that the river Saraswati dried up and vanished beneath the earth at the desert pilgrimage site known as Vinasana.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Data from the Wide Field Sensor (WiFS) of Indian Remote Sensing Satellite, IRS, which has a spatial resolution of 188 m and a swath of 810 km, has been used for mapping prominent palaeo channels.
facts.text: ISRO scientists mapped extensive subsurface palaeochannel networks in northwestern India using wide-field sensor satellite imagery with a spatial resolution of 188 metres.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Saraswati Nadi in Haryana and its linkage with the Vedic Saraswati River - Integrated study based on satellite images and ground based information.
facts.source_name: ISRO / Journal of the Geological Society of India
facts.text: An integrated satellite remote sensing and field investigation published by ISRO scientists linked the modern seasonal Sarsuti stream in Haryana to the wider buried Vedic Saraswati palaeodrainage network.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Diversion of the Sutlej out of the Ghaggar palaeochannel occurred much earlier, between ~10 and 8 ka, before urban Indus settlement.
facts.text: Geomorphological and dating research published in Nature Communications revealed that the Sutlej River had diverted away from the Ghaggar channel by 8000 years ago, well before urban Harappan settlements developed along its banks.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Romila Thapar declares the identification of the Ghaggar with the Saraswati controversial, while Rajesh Kochhar argues that early references to the Saraswati could be the Haraxvati plain in Afghanistan.
facts.source_name: The Vedic People (Rajesh Kochhar) / Academic Indology
facts.text: Scholars dispute whether the Rigvedic Saraswati corresponds to the Ghaggar-Hakra bed in India or originally described the Helmand River in Afghanistan before the toponym migrated eastwards.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Popular tradition holds that the Saraswati flows invisibly underground to join the holy Ganga and Yamuna rivers at the sacred Triveni Sangam.
facts.text: Popular folk belief asserts that after disappearing into the desert sand, the Saraswati continues to flow as a hidden underground stream to emerge at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna at Prayagraj.
